messages:
marta_support: Hey team — customer Greenline reported a wire was returned by the beneficiary bank. They say funds were bounced and invoice INV-2025-0912 is now overdue. Return reason from the bank: "Invalid account/branch combination".
ryan_payments: Do we have the raw outgoing wire payload? need to check if we sent a branch code in the remittance or wrong SWIFT.
marta_support: Attached the outgoing payload we sent via the /payments/wire API earlier today (txn id tx_8F9a2).
```
{
  "tx_id": "tx_8F9a2",
  "customer_id": "cust_greenline",
  "invoice_id": "INV-2025-0912",
  "amount": "12500.00",
  "currency": "USD",
  "beneficiary": {
    "name": "Greenline Logistics Europe",
    "account_number": "12345678-001",
    "iban": "GB82 WEST 1234 5698 7654 32",
    "swift": "NWBKGB2L",
    "branch_code": "001"
  },
  "remittance_info": "PO: 7789 - INV-2025-0912"
}
```
kai_infra: Hmm — looks like the bank's account_number is a base account + branch suffix. Some recipient banks expect the branch to be a separate field or encoded differently in the IBAN/SWIFT. If the branch_code was appended to the account_number we might have sent an invalid combination.
ryan_payments: The beneficiary's IBAN is GB — the IBAN itself already encodes branch details sometimes; mixing both can confuse correspondent banks. Did our normalization step strip non-digit chars? our serializer left the dash in account_number.
marta_support: Right — the API call included the raw account string with a dash. Customer copy-pasted from their internal invoice which uses account-branch format.
jules_ops: Customer-facing ask: can we retry the wire today? Finance needs confirmation before we re-initiate and they want to know if we need to change the payload.
ryan_payments: Proposed remediation: 1) Contact beneficiary bank to confirm expected account format (separate branch vs appended). 2) If branch should be separate, set beneficiary.account_number to 12345678 and add beneficiary.branch_code = 001 and regenerate the IBAN (or leave IBAN blank if bank requires local account). 3) Use our correspondent bank fallback with SWIFT augmented: NWBKGB2LXXX (include branch characters) and set instruction_code=CHQ if required by bank.
marta_support: I called the customer's AP team — they confirmed their bank uses separate branch field and that the IBAN is valid but their domestic rails require account=12345678 and branch=001. They want us to retry under their authorization.
billing-bot: NOTE: Retrying will create a new settlement attempt. If successful, invoice INV-2025-0912 will be marked paid and fees will apply per normal settled transfers.
kai_infra: Quick engineering note: our wire serializer should normalize account numbers by removing punctuation before sending, and we should validate that account+branch maps to the provided IBAN checksum. I can add a pre-flight validation hook to flag mismatches (fail-fast) — low-risk change.
ryan_payments: For immediate unblocking: ops can re-send tx as new_tx_9B1c4 with sanitized account fields. I can draft the exact payload.
marta_support: Customer gave written approval for retry. @ryan_payments please proceed once ops confirms the sanitized payload.
ryan_payments: Will do. Draft payload and post here for sign-off.
```
{
  "tx_id": "new_tx_9B1c4",
  "beneficiary": {
    "account_number": "12345678",
    "branch_code": "001",
    "iban": "GB82WEST12345698765432",
    "swift": "NWBKGB2LXXX"
  }
}
```
jules_ops: Signed off from ops. Please note to select correspondent_bank: "LloydsIntermediary" to avoid intermediary strip.
ryan_payments: Sending to payments queue now, tagging this thread with tx id new_tx_9B1c4. I'll monitor with the bank and update on status.
marta_support: Thanks. I'll update the customer with ETA and log the delay reason as "account+branch mismatch" for postmortem. :white_check_mark:
ryan_payments: Update: payment acknowledged by correspondent (ACK received). If it clears, final status should be settled within 2 business days. I'll post final confirmation or return reason here.
